Asymptotic Variance of Maintainability

Source: R/04_main.R
vcov_main.Rd

Compute the pointwise asymptotic variance of the plug-in maintainability estimator for an irreducible finite-state Markov chain, treating the initial distribution as fixed.

Usage

vcov_main(x, time, down)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A single nonnegative integer giving the discrete time point. Values must be less than .Machine$integer.max; missing and infinite values are not allowed.

down

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the non-operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric scalar containing the variance in the \(\sqrt{n}\) limit of the maintainability estimator. Divide by the number of observed transitions \(n\) to approximate the variance of the estimator itself. This is a pointwise variance, not a joint covariance across times.

Details

Since \(\widehat M(t) - M(t) = -(\widehat Q(t) - Q(t))\), the asymptotic variance of maintainability equals that of down-state survival. Proposition 10 of Gavrilopoulos, Trevezas, and Votsi (2026) states this sign change after Equation (54). The variance is obtained from Equation (52) with the down-state block substituted for the operational block. This function calls vcov_dssc() without changing its result. The full-chain stationary distribution is used and the variance at time zero is zero.

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161.

See also

main(), vcov_dssc(), vcov_main_sl()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0, 1), P)
main(x, time = 0:3, down = 2L)
#> [1] 0.000 0.300 0.510 0.657
vcov_main(x, time = 3L, down = 2L)
#> [1] 1.134472
vcov_main_sl(x, time = 3L, down = 2L)
#> [1] 1.134472
